questions.question: The number of vertebrae in a human is ___.
questions.explanation: The number of vertebrae in adult human is 26.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Symbiotic association between fungi and algae are called ___.
questions.explanation: Lichens are symbiotic associations i.e. mutually useful associations, between algae and fungi. Mycorrhiza are associations between fungi and roots of higher plants.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Cell theory was formulated by ___.
questions.explanation: Cell theory was formulated by Schleiden and Schwann.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following are characteristics of prokaryotic cells? (a) Ribosomes are made of 50S and 30S subunits (b) They can have plasmids (c) They contain mesosome (d) They have peroxisomes
questions.explanation: The following are characteristics of prokaryotic cells. Ribosomes are made of 50S and 30S subunits (70S Ribosomes) • They can have plasmids (Extra chromosomal DNA) • They contain mesosome (Infoldings of plasma membrane) - They do not possess membrane bound organelles such as peroxisomes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following is not a part of human central neural system?
questions.explanation: Pericardium is a double walled membranous bag that protects the heart. Arachnoid, dura mater and pia mater are meninges, which cover the brain inside the skull.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Mitochondrial inner membrane encloses ___.
questions.explanation: Mitochondrial inner membrane encloses matrix.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II. A. | Cristae | I. | Flat membrane sacs in stroma of chloroplast B. | Cisternae | II. | Infoldings in mitochondria C. | Thylakoids | III. | Cell membrane D. | Phospholipid | IV. | Disc shaped sacs in the Golgi apparatus
questions.explanation: Following are the correct matches: A. | Cristae | II. | Infoldings in mitochondria B. | Cisternae | IV. | Disc shaped sacs in the Golgi apparatus C. | Thylakoids | I. | Flat membrane sacs in stroma of chloroplast D. | Phospholipid | III. | Cell membrane
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The plastid that stores xanthophyll is known as ___.
questions.explanation: The plastid that stores xanthophyll is known as chromoplast.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements related to pituitary gland are correct? (a) It is divided anatomically into adenohypophysis and neurohypophysis (b) It secretes follicle stimulating hormone (c) It secretes melanocyte stimulating hormone (d) It does not secrete prolactin
questions.explanation: Adenohypophysis of pituitary gland also secrets prolactin.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Photorespiration reaction catalyzed by RuBisCo is shown below: RuBP + O₂ → 3-Phosphoglycerate + X. Identify "X" from the given options:
questions.explanation: During the process of photorespiration, RuBP binds with O $ _{2} $ and RuBP instead of being converted to 2 molecules of PGA, forms one molecule each of phosphoglycerate and phosphoglycolate. Hence, in the given reaction, the "X" is 2-phosphoglycolate.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Mad cow disease is caused by _____.
questions.explanation: Mad cow disease is caused by prions.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which pigment has absorption peak at 700 nm in the photosynthetic reaction centre PSI (P700)?
questions.explanation: In PSI, the reaction centre chlorophyll a has an absorption peak at 700 nm and hence, is called $ P_{700} $.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In water, frogs respire using _____.
questions.explanation: Frogs respire on land and in water by different methods. In water, skin acts as aquatic respiratory organ (cutaneous respiration). Dissolved oxygen in the water is exchanged through the skin by diffusion. On land, the buccal cavity, skin and lungs act as the respiratory organs.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of arrangement of bones in the lower limb of humans?
questions.explanation: Each hindlimb consists of 30 bones. The bones of the lower limb is femur (thigh bone). A cup shaped bone called patella cover the knee ventrally (knee cap). tibia and fibula, tarsals (ankle bones), metatarsals and phalanges. - So, the correct sequence of arrangement of bones in the lower limb of humans will be Femur - patella - tibia - tarsal.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Phyllotaxy is the pattern of arrangement of ___.
questions.explanation: Phyllotaxy is the pattern of arrangement of leaves on the stem.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II. A. | Starch | I. | Fights infection B. | Antibody | II. | Energy storage C. | Concanavalin A | III. | Glucose transport D. | Glut-4 | IV. | Lectin
questions.explanation: Starch $ \rightarrow $ Energy storage Antibody $ \rightarrow $ Fights infection Concanavalin A $ \rightarrow $ Lectin Glut-4 $ \rightarrow $ Glucose transport
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Given below are two statements : Statement I: When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry. itemment II : In phylum Echinodermata, both adults and larvae are radially symmetrical. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
questions.option_a: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.option_b: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.option_c: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.option_d: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry. The members of the phylum Echinodermata exhibit radial or bilateral symmetry depending on the stage. Adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical while larval echinoderms are bilaterally symmetrical.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Endomembrane system includes ___.
questions.option_a: endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuole
questions.option_b: endoplasmic reticulum, chloroplast, peroxisomes and vacuole
questions.option_d: Golgi complex, chloroplast, peroxisomes and vacuole
options: endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuole
endoplasmic reticulum, chloroplast, peroxisomes and vacuole
Golgi complex, chloroplast, peroxisomes and vacuole
questions.explanation: Endomembrane system includes organelles whose functions are coordinated. It includes total four organelles, namely Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi body, vacuole and lysosomes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are produced at the end of glycolysis from 206 molecules of glucose?
questions.explanation: Two molecules of pyruvic acid are formed at the end of glycolysis from one molecule of glucose. From 206 molecules of glucose, 412 molecules of pyruvic acid are formed.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following plant growth regulators is used as herbicide?
questions.explanation: 2, 4-D is an artificial auxin, which is widely used as herbicide.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In gymnosperms, the male and female gametophytes remain within the sporangia. Statement II: In gymnosperms, seeds are not covered. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.option_a: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.option_b: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.option_c: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.option_d: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: In gymnosperm, the male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence. They remain within sporangia, retained on the sporophyte. In gymnosperms the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilisation. The seeds that develop post fertilisation, are not covered, i.e., naked.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II. A. | Spherical | I. | Vibrio B. | Rod | II. | Cocci C. | Comma | III. | Spirilla D. | Spirillum | IV. | Bacilli
questions.explanation: Bacteria are grouped under four categories based on their shape : Spherical $ \rightarrow $ Coccus Rod-shaped $ \rightarrow $ Bacillus Comma-shaped $ \rightarrow $ Vibrium Spiral $ \rightarrow $ Spirillum
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following are characteristic features of Solanaceae family? (a) Flowers are bisexual and actinomorphic (b) Calyx have five sepals and are united (c) Androecium have five stamens and are epipetalous (d) Ovary is inferior
questions.explanation: In Solanaceae family, flowers are bisexual and actinomorphic. Calyx include five sepals that are united. Androecium include five stamens and it is epipetalous. Ovary is superior.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Select the correct sequence of experiments that led to a gradual understanding of photosynthesis in green plants.
questions.option_a: Absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b → production of glucose → release of oxygen → role of air
questions.option_b: Role of air $ \rightarrow $ release of oxygen $ \rightarrow $ production of glucose $ \rightarrow $ absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
questions.option_c: Release of oxygen $ \rightarrow $ production of glucose $ \rightarrow $ absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b $ \rightarrow $ role of air
questions.option_d: Production of glucose $ \rightarrow $ role of air $ \rightarrow $ release of oxygen $ \rightarrow $ absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
options: Absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b → production of glucose → release of oxygen → role of air
Role of air $ \rightarrow $ release of oxygen $ \rightarrow $ production of glucose $ \rightarrow $ absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
Release of oxygen $ \rightarrow $ production of glucose $ \rightarrow $ absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b $ \rightarrow $ role of air
Production of glucose $ \rightarrow $ role of air $ \rightarrow $ release of oxygen $ \rightarrow $ absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
questions.explanation: Following is the appropriate sequence of experiments that led to a gradual understanding of photosynthesis in green plants. Role of air in Glucose (Joseph Priestley's bell jar experiment) 1770 ↓ Release of oxygen (Jan Ingenhousz's experiment using aquatic plant) ↓ Production of Glucose (Julius Von Sach's experiment) 1854 ↓ Absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b (T.W. Engelmann's experiment)
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The number of action potentials generated by sino-atrial node (SAN) in a healthy human is ___ per minute.
questions.explanation: The number of action potentials generated by sino-atrial node (SAN) in a healthy human is 70 - 75 per minute.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: How many turns of Calvin cycle are required for the formation of three molecules of glucose?
questions.explanation: To make one molecule of glucose 6 turns of the cycle are required. Therefore, for the formation of three molecules of glucose, $ 6 \times 3 = 18 $, turns of Calvin cycle are required.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
questions.option_a: Blood coagulates in response to an injury
options: Blood coagulates in response to an injury
questions.explanation: Fibrins are formed by the conversion of inactive fibrinogen in the plasma by the enzyme thrombin.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II. A. | Family | I. | Sapindales B. | Genus | II. | Dicotyledonae C. | Class | III. | Anacardiaceae D. | Phylum | IV. | Angiospermae E. | Order | V. | Mangifera
questions.explanation: (Conceptual errata) Mangifera represents Genus, Anacardiaceae represents family, Sapindales represents order, Dicotyledonae represents class, Phylum Angiospermae [correct should be division]
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Arrange the following taxonomic categories in ascending order. (a) Genus (b) Class (c) Order (d) Phylum (e) Family (f) Kingdom (g) Species
questions.explanation: The following is the arrangement of taxonomic categories in ascending order. Species (g), Genus (a), Family (e), Order (c), Class (b), Phylum (d), Kingdom (f).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II. A. | Marginal placentation | I. | Argemone B. | Axile placentation | II. | Tomato C. | Parietal placentation | III. | Primrose D. | Free central placentation | IV. | Pea
questions.explanation: Marginal placentation - Pea Axile placentation - Tomato Parietal placentation - Argemone Free central placentation - Primrose
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sphenopsida class belongs to _____.
questions.explanation: Sphenopsida class belongs to pteridophytes.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding photorespiration are correct? (a) Do not occur in C3 plants (b) $ CO_{2} $ is consumed and $ O_{2} $ is generated (c) Phosphoglycolate is formed (d) No synthesis of ATP and NADPH
questions.explanation: • Photorespiration can occur in C3 plants. - In photorespiration, $ O_{2} $ is consumed and $ CO_{2} $ is released. - Phosphoglycolate is formed as the initial product. There is no synthesis of ATP and NADPH in photorespiration.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum ___.
questions.option_a: has ribosomes attached to its surface
questions.option_b: is the major site for the synthesis of lipids
questions.option_c: is actively involved in protein synthesis
questions.option_d: is a site for the synthesis of carbohydrates
options: has ribosomes attached to its surface
is the major site for the synthesis of lipids
is actively involved in protein synthesis
is a site for the synthesis of carbohydrates
questions.explanation: The Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) is responsible for synthesis of lipids as well as steroidal hormones. It is not associated with ribosomes and hence appears smooth. Rough endoplasmic reticulum is actively involved in protein synthesis. Carbohydrate synthesis occurs in chloroplasts.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
questions.explanation: The two main types of cells in the Islet of Langerhans are called $ \alpha $-cells and $ \beta $-cells. The $ \alpha $-cells secrete a hormone called glucagon, while the $ \beta $-cells secrete insulin. Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis while insulin stimulates glycogenesis.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Genus represents _____.
questions.option_b: a population of plants and animals
questions.option_c: a group of closely related species
questions.option_d: a group of closely related families
options: a population of plants and animals
a group of closely related species
a group of closely related families
questions.explanation: Genus comprises a group of related species which has more characters in common in comparison to species of other genera.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following is not a prokaryote?
questions.explanation: The prokaryotic cells are represented by bacteria, blue-green algae, Mycoplasma and PPLO. Fungi are eukaryotic organisms.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following plant growth regulators promotes internode elongation prior to flowering in cabbage?
questions.explanation: Gibberellin promotes internode elongation prior to flowering in cabbage.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The correct sequence of adult cell cycle phases is ___.
questions.explanation: Gap1 phase is the first phase of interphase. After Gap1 phase, synthesis phase starts in which DNA replicates, then Gap2 phase occurs and finally cell cycle ends with M phase (mitosis).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II. A. | Fusion of protoplasms between gametes | I. | Meiosis B. | Fusion of two nuclei | II. | Plasmogamy C. | Generation of haploid spores | III. | Karyogamy
questions.explanation: Karyogamy involve fusion of two nuclei. Plasmogamy is fusion of protoplasm. Meiosis leads to the production of haploid spores.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The class name Reptilia refers to creeping or crawling mode of locomotion. Statement II: All organisms belonging to Reptilia have three chambered heart. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.option_a: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.option_b: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.option_c: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.option_d: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: The class Reptilia refers to their creeping or crawling mode of locomotion. Heart is usually three-chambered, but four-chambered in crocodiles. So, All organisms belonging to class Reptilia does not possess three chambered heart.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Given below are two statements : Statement I: Chromosomes are fully condensed at the end of prophase I. Statement II : Meiosis I resembles mitosis. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.option_a: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.option_b: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.option_c: Statement I is correct, but Statement II is false
questions.option_d: Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is true
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is true
questions.explanation: The final stage of meiotic prophase-I is diakinesis. So, at the end of prophase-I the chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled to prepare the homologous chromosomes for separation. So, Statement I is correct. Meiosis II resembles mitosis as it is an equational division.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following is not a characteristic of chordates?
questions.explanation: The members of phylum Chordata shows following features at any stage of life. (1) Presence of notochord (2) Pharynx perforated by gill slits (3) Dorsal, hollow and single central nervous system (4) Ventral heart (5) A post-anal tail Gill slits are absent in non-chordates.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Length of the stem at time 0 is 20 cm. The arithmetic growth rate is 30 cm per day. What is the length of the stem at the end of the $ 7^{th} $ day?
questions.explanation: Arithmetic growth can be expressed as : $ L_{t}=L_{0}+rt $ [where, $ L_{t}=length\ at\ time't', L_{0}=Length\ at\ time'zero', r=growth\ rate] $ L_{7th\ day} \Rightarrow 20 + 30 \times 7 $ $ \Rightarrow $ 20 + 210 $ \Rightarrow $ 230 cm The length of the stem at the end of $ 7^{th} $ day is 230 cm.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Arrange the following elements in descending order of their contribution to percentage weight of the human body. (a) Oxygen (b) Carbon (c) Hydrogen (d) Nitrogen
questions.explanation: The arrangement of elements in descending order of their contribution to percentage weight of the human body is Oxygen (65%) → Carbon (18.5%) → Hydrogen (9.5%) → Nitrogen (3.3%)
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: In frogs, the number of pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain are ___.
questions.explanation: In frogs, there are ten pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following is used as a clot buster?
questions.explanation: Streptokinase produced by the bacterium Streptococcus and modified by genetic engineering is used as a 'clot-buster' for removing clots from the blood vessels of patients who have undergone myocardial infarction leading to heart attack.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The inactive form of Bt toxin is converted to the active form in the insect gut ___
questions.explanation: Bt toxin protein exists as inactive protoxins, but once an insect ingests the inactive toxin, it is converted into an active form of toxin due to the alkaline pH of the gut which solubilises the crystals.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Given below are two statements : Statement I: Down's syndrome is caused by the absence of one of the X-chromosomes. Statement II : Turner's syndrome is caused by the presence of an additional copy of the chromosomes. In the light of the above statements,
questions.option_a: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.option_b: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.option_c: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.option_d: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.explanation: The cause of genetic disorder-Down's syndrome is the presence of an additional copy of the chromosome number 21 (Trisomy 21). The cause of genetic disorder-Turner's syndrome is the absence of one of the X-chromosomes; i.e. 45 with X0.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following disease is not sexually transmitted?
questions.explanation: Genital warts, syphilis and gonorrhoea are sexually transmitted diseases. Genital warts is caused by Human papilloma virus. Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum. Gonorrhoea is caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Tuberculosis is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. This disease spreads through air.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sperm motility is due to ___.
questions.explanation: Sperm travels across the fallopian tube via flagellar movement.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Natural selection can lead to ___. (a) stabilisation (b) genetic drift (c) directional change (d) disruption
questions.explanation: Natural selection can lead to stabilization, directional change or disruption. Natural selection is a process in which heritable variations enabling better survival enabled to reproduce and leave greater number of progeny. A critical analysis makes us believe that variation due to mutation or recombination during gametogenesis or due to gene flow or genetic drift results in changed frequency of genes and alleles in future generation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The method of directly or injecting a sperm into ovum in assisted reproductive technology is called:
questions.explanation: Intra cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) is a procedure to form an embryo in the laboratory in which a sperm is directly injected into the ovum. ZIFT (Zygote intra fallopian transfer) involves transfer of the zygote or early embryos with upto 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube. GIFT (Gamete intra fallopian transfer) involves transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce one, but can provide suitable environment for fertilisation and further development.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following structure is not a part of the male reproductive system?
questions.explanation: The male sex accessory ducts include rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis and vas deferens. The oviducts, uterus and vagina constitute the female accessory ducts. Infundibulum is the part of oviduct.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Arrange the following in descending order of number of species in the Amazonian rain forest. (a) Plants (b) Birds (c) Fishes (d) Invertebrates (e) Mammals
questions.explanation: The Amazonian rain forest is home to more than 40,000 species of plants, 3,000 of fishes, 1300 of birds, 427 of mammals, 378 of reptiles and of more than 1,25,000 invertebrates. Hence the correct decreasing order would be (d)>(a)>(c)>(b)>(e)
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Ovulation is caused by LH surge leading to rupture of Graafian follicles. Statement II: Graafian follicle remaining after ovulation transform into corpus luteum and secretes large amount of estrogen. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.option_a: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.option_b: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.option_c: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.option_d: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Rapid secretion of LH leading to its maximum level during the mid-cycle called LH surge induces rupture of Graafian follicle and thereby the release of ovum (ovulation). The remaining parts of the Graafian follicle transform as the corpus luteum, which secretes large amounts of progesterone.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following are primary consumers in a food chain?
questions.explanation: Primary consumers in a food chain are the herbivores.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: A population of diploid organisms is at Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. If the frequency of allele A is 0.1, the frequency of AA is ___.
questions.explanation: The frequency of allele A(p) = 0.1 As per the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, Frequency of AA = p^{2} = (0.1)^{2} = 0.01
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II. (A) Excess growth hormone (B) Luteinizing hormone (C) Vasopressin (D) Oxytocin List-I List-II (I) Reabsorption of water and electrolytes in kidney (II) Contraction of uterus during child birth (III) Acromegaly (IV) Ovulation
questions.explanation: Excess ground. egaly es in kidneys
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle is guarded by _____.
questions.explanation: The opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle is guarded by a valve formed of three muscular flaps or cusps, called the tricuspid valve. A bicuspid/mitral valve guards the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle. The openings of the right and the left ventricles into the pulmonary artery and the aorta, respectively, are provided with the semilunar valves.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Sponges exchange $ O_{2} $ with $ CO_{2} $ by ___.
questions.option_a: simple diffusion over their entire body surfaces
options: simple diffusion over their entire body surfaces
questions.explanation: Mechanisms of breathing vary among different groups of animals depending mainly on their habitats and levels of organisation. Lower invertebrates like sponges, coelenterates, flatworms, etc., exchange $ O_{2} $ with $ CO_{2} $ by simple diffusion over their entire body surfaces. Earthworms use their moist cuticle and insects have a network of tubes (tracheal tubes) to transport atmospheric air within the body. Gills are used by most of the aquatic arthropods and molluscs.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: How many theca are present in each lobe of a typical bilobed angiosperm anther?
questions.explanation: A typical anther is bilobed with each lobe having two theca i.e. they are dithecous.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system by the release of ___.
questions.explanation: Muscle concraction is initiated by a signal sent by the central nervous system (CNS) via a motor neuron. The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre is called the neuromuscular junction or motor-end plate. A neural signal reaching this junction releases a neurotransmitter (Acetylcholine) which generates an action potential in the sarcolemma.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about lac-operon is correct?
questions.option_b: Lactose activates repressor to bind to the operator
questions.option_c: Genes i, z, y and a share single common promoter
questions.option_d: Galactose can act as an inducer of lac operon
options: Lactose activates repressor to bind to the operator
Genes i, z, y and a share single common promoter
Galactose can act as an inducer of lac operon
questions.explanation: Galactose cannot act as an inducer of lac operon. Gene i is constitutively expressed in lac operon. Repressor binds to the operator when the lactose is not available. Genes z, y and a are structural genes and have a different promoter than that of the i gene.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following in female gametophyte of an angiosperm helps in guiding the pollen tube for fertilizing the eggs?
questions.explanation: Synergids guide the entry of pollen tube for fertilizing the eggs, in a typical angiospermic embryo sac.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following plant produces non-albuminous seeds?
questions.explanation: S01. Non-albuminous seeds have no residual endosperm as it is completely consumed during embryo development. E.g. Pea. Wheat, maize and barley are the examples of albuminous seeds.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: If the diploid chromosome number of typical angiosperm is 36, what would be the chromosome number in its endosperm?
questions.explanation: The endosperm is triploid, if the diploid chromosome number of typical angiosperm is 36 i.e. 2n = 36 then n = 18 So, $ 3n = n + n + n $ = 18 + 18 + 18 = 54
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the reabsorption process in Henle's loop are correct? (a) The descending limb of Henle's loop is permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes. (b) Urine gets concentrated in Henle's loop. (c) Reabsorption of Na⁺ and water takes place in Henle's loop. (d) Active or passive transport of electrolytes occurs in the ascending limb of Henle's loop.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct order of arrangement of vertebrate column from the head to toe?
questions.option_a: Cervical vertebra, thoracic vertebra, sacrum, lumbar vertebra
questions.option_b: Sacrum, lumbar vertebra, thoracic vertebra, cervical vertebra
questions.option_c: Cervical vertebra, lumbar vertebra, thoracic vertebra, sacrum
questions.option_d: Cervical vertebra, thoracic vertebra, lumbar vertebra, sacrum
options: Cervical vertebra, thoracic vertebra, sacrum, lumbar vertebra
Sacrum, lumbar vertebra, thoracic vertebra, cervical vertebra
Cervical vertebra, lumbar vertebra, thoracic vertebra, sacrum
Cervical vertebra, thoracic vertebra, lumbar vertebra, sacrum
questions.explanation: The vertebral column is formed by 26 serially arranged units called vertebrae and is dorsally placed. The vertebral column is differentiated into cervical (7), thoracic (12), lumbar (5), sacral (1-fused) and coccygeal (1-fused) regions starting from the skull. So, the correct sequence will be: Cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacrum and coccyx.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: Which of the following is not evidence for evolution?
questions.option_a: Convergent evolution of traits like wings of birds and butterflies
questions.option_c: Embryological support for evolution as proposed by Ernst Heckel
questions.option_d: Divergent evolution of anatomical structures such as forelimbs
options: Convergent evolution of traits like wings of birds and butterflies
Embryological support for evolution as proposed by Ernst Heckel
Divergent evolution of anatomical structures such as forelimbs
questions.explanation: Divergent evolution of anatomical structures, such as forelimbs, indicate homology. Homology indicates common ancestry and acts as the evidence of evolution. When same structure develops along different directions due to adaptation to different needs, they are called homologous structures. Convergent evolution does not act as the evidence for evolution, because species can develop similar features without a common ancestor. Fossils are remains of hard parts of life-forms found in rocks. A study of fossils in different sedimentary layers indicates the geological period in which they existed. Embryological support for evolution was proposed by Ernst Heckel based upon the observation of certain features during embryonic stage common to all vertebrates that are absent in adult. But later, this proposal was disapproved on careful study performed by Karl Ernst von Baer.

questions.question: Consider a population of 10 million cells. Given the per-capita birth rate of 0.002 (per unit time) and the per-capita death rate of 0.002 (per unit time), the expected number of cells after 10 generations is ___.
questions.explanation: The per-capita birth rate of bacteria is 0.002. The per-capita death rate of bacteria is 0.002. The population dynamic equation is $ \frac{dN}{dt}=(b-d)N $ Since $ r=(b-d)=0.002-0.002=0 $ $ \frac{dN}{dt}=0 $ So, the population remains constant at all times. Thus, even after 10 generations, the expected number of cells will be 10 million.

questions.question: Which of the following statements are Correct? (a) Energy flow from producers to consumers is unidirectional (b) Energy pyramid can never be inverted (c) Transfer of energy follows the 1% law
questions.explanation: Energy flow is unidirectional. First plants capture solar energy and then, food is transferred from the producers to decomposers. Pyramid of energy is always upright. It can never be inverted, because when energy flows from a particular trophic level to the next trophic level, some energy is always lost as heat at each step. The transfer of energy follows 10 per cent law - only 10 per cent of the energy is transferred to each trophic level from the lower trophic level.
